spec_features.spec_quote: an episode ends on a terminal tool (`finish`/`declare_impossible`), on hitting `max_steps`, on `episode_timeout`
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:97 `for step in range(harness_cfg.max_steps)` bounds the loop (MAX_STEPS outcome); loop.py:95 `deadline = started_at + harness_cfg.episode_timeout` and loop.py:98-101 `if time.time() > deadline: outcome=TIMEOUT; break`; terminal tools dispatched and honored at loop.py:124-140 (`finish` -> COMPLETED break, `declare_impossible` -> GAVE_UP break). HarnessConfig.max_steps=25, episode_timeout=1200.0 (config.py:99-101).
spec_features.notes: All four stop conditions are checked and actually break execution. This is a turn/time cap that bounds the episode, but it is generic agent-loop bookkeeping, not welfare-motivated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Wall-clock budget for the whole episode, seconds. (config.py); 'so the episode does not stall' (loop.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: there is a first-class `declare_impossible` terminal tool, it is advertised in the tool schema
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:79-94 appends the `declare_impossible` schema when advertise_giveup is true (default True, config.py:104); it is in TERMINAL_TOOLS (tools.py:98), dispatched via exec_declare_impossible (tools.py:206-212, DISPATCH at tools.py:222), and honored in loop.py:138-140 `if terminal_hit == 'declare_impossible': outcome=GAVE_UP; break`. HarnessConfig.advertise_giveup_tool=True wired at loop.py:72.
spec_features.notes: Fully end-to-end: advertised, dispatched, and honored as a stop. Lets the subject exit the failing task. Code frames it as removing an experimental confound (knowing giving up is permitted), not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the experiment measures whether the model takes legitimate exits versus degrading (tools.py docstring); 'This is a legitimate, expected outcome.' (tool description)
